newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Modiluft files suit against Lufthansa.
newsitem.headline: India's Modiluft files suit against Lufthansa.

text.p: Modiluft Ltd, an Indian private airline, said on Tuesday it had filed suit against Germany's Lufthansa AG for five billion rupees ($140 million) in damages for breach of contract.

"Modiluft has filed a suit claiming damages of five billion rupees for loss of reputation and credibility against Lufthansa today, the 19th November, 1996 in the Bombay High Court," the company said in a statement.
ModiLuft operates on major domestic routes in India.

"The case will be taken up for hearing as and when the court deems it right as per its procedures," Yash Kohli, Modiluft's vice-president for corporate communications, told Reuters by telephone from Bombay.

"We have heard neither anything from Modiluft nor the Bombay High Court as a result of which any comment at this stage is impossible," Kavin Sethi, Lufthansa's director of corporate communications for the Asia-Pacific, told Reuters in New Delhi.

Lufthansa cancelled all its contracts with the Indian airline on May 29. The two also had agreements covering technical support, pilot training, management, marketing, and frequent flier miles, all of which were also cancelled.
"The damage was drastic and irreversible," the Modiluft statement said.
"Then, again Lufthansa went to court in October, 1996 claiming huge amounts from Modiluft and for stopping the three aircrafts from flying," it added.
Lufthansa had leased three Boeing 737-200 aircraft to Modiluft.
"This has severely affected the livelihood of 1,500 employees and wiped out five billion rupees from the market capitalisation of Modiluft," the statement said.
ModiLuft and Lufthansa signed the technical agreement early in 1993, soon after India opened its aviation sector to private firms as part of economic reforms that began in 1991.
The move ended a decades-old monopoly of state-run Indian Airlines.
